reviewCadence: At feature design, before release gates, and after every security-significant incident.

features.name: Account authentication
features.description: Password, passkey, MFA, session creation, recovery, and account onboarding flows.

features.name: Tenant and team authorization
features.description: Tenant, team, membership, role, and delegated actor authorization boundaries.

features.name: Browser mutating requests
features.description: Cookie-authenticated web requests, security headers, and browser request protections.

features.name: Web hygiene and rendering
features.description: Browser security headers, CSP, frame-ancestors, and clickjacking protections.

features.name: Email and webhook ingestion
features.description: Email dispatch, delivery webhook signatures, and Trust/Risk evaluation.

features.name: Billing and payment webhooks
features.description: Inbound Stripe webhooks, signature validation, idempotency, and replay protection.

features.name: Platform operations
features.description: Cockpit operator authentication, privileged mutations, role permissions, and idempotency.

features.name: Audit, monitoring, and supply chain
features.description: Append-only audit evidence, detection coverage, dependency coverage, and secret scanning.

countermeasures.name: Authentication throttling and bot friction
countermeasures.description: IP and action-based rate limits, timing-safe verification, and risk event recording.

countermeasures.name: MFA and step-up abuse controls
countermeasures.description: TOTP windowing, single-use replay prevention, and step-up requirements for sensitive actions.

countermeasures.name: Team and workspace scope enforcement
countermeasures.description: Tenant, team, workspace, delegated actor, role, and ownership boundaries.

countermeasures.name: Security headers and request guards
countermeasures.description: Strict transport security, clear-site-data on logout, and origin protection.

countermeasures.name: Security headers and clickjacking controls
countermeasures.description: CSP frame-ancestors, X-Frame-Options, strict content type, referrer, and permissions policies.

countermeasures.name: Reviewed safe rendering and CSP guardrails
countermeasures.description: Strict Content-Security-Policy default-src none, script and style restrictions.

countermeasures.name: Ingestion and webhook verification controls
countermeasures.description: Cryptographic signature verification, message age checking, and rate limiting on ingress.

countermeasures.name: Webhook authenticity and replay controls
countermeasures.description: Raw payload signature verification, payload hashing, duplicate handling, and advisory transaction locks.

countermeasures.name: Platform operations privileged action gates
countermeasures.description: Permission checks, operator session validation, idempotency keys, and advisory locks.

countermeasures.name: Audit immutability
countermeasures.description: Audit event tables and structured logging across services.

countermeasures.name: Supply chain and secret scanning
countermeasures.description: Repository checks for secrets, dependency coverage, SBOM evidence, container checks, and license boundaries.

abuseCases.attack: An attacker automates credential stuffing, password spraying, registration abuse, or authentication probes.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP A2 Broken Authentication; OWASP Automated Threats

abuseCases.attack: An attacker brute-forces MFA, abuses recovery paths, or keeps retrying failed step-up flows to take over an account.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP Multifactor Authentication; OWASP A2 Broken Authentication

abuseCases.attack: An authenticated actor manipulates team, workspace, or resource identifiers to access or mutate another customer's resources.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP A5 Broken Access Control; OWASP IDOR

abuseCases.attack: An attacker triggers browser-level authenticated mutations or bypasses security headers through forged requests or missing transport protections.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP CSRF Prevention; OWASP A5 Broken Access Control

abuseCases.attack: An attacker frames privileged UI, clickjacks account actions, or exploits missing browser hardening headers.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP Clickjacking Defense; OWASP A6 Security Misconfiguration

abuseCases.attack: An attacker attempts cross-site scripting (XSS) through malicious input injection or missing content security policies.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP A7 Cross-Site Scripting; OWASP Content Security Policy

abuseCases.attack: An attacker sends forged SNS notification payloads or abuses worker dispatch pipelines with tampered delivery receipts.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP API Security; OWASP Message Authenticity

abuseCases.attack: An attacker sends fake, tampered, stale, or duplicate webhook payloads to trigger illegitimate billing side effects.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP Webhook Security; OWASP A5 Broken Access Control

abuseCases.attack: A compromised, confused, or overprivileged operator attempts irreversible platform mutations without proper role, idempotency, or permission context.
An attacker alters or deletes audit evidence to hide account, billing, or administrative abuse.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP A10 Insufficient Logging and Monitoring

abuseCases.attack: An attacker exploits leaked secrets, unknown vulnerable dependencies, missing SBOM evidence, or weak container/dependency hygiene.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP A9 Vulnerable Components; OWASP Software Supply Chain Security
